tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: During the Financial year 2023-24, the company has received a consolidated GST demand for an amount of ₹ 161.79 million (excluding penalty and interest) for the period July 2017 to March 2021. The company has disputed these demand and had filed a writ petition before the Madras High Court. A interim stay has been obtained on all further proceedings until the matter is heard.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Additional Commissioner, Office of Commissioner of Goods and Service Tax and Central Excise, Salem
tax_litigation.status: In the Interim Stay period granted by the Hon'ble High Court of Madras

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: a) During the Financial year 2024-25, the company has received a GST demand for an amount of ₹ 50.41 million (excluding penalty and interest). The demand related to short payment of GST due to wrong classification of goods, short payment of GST under RCM, irregular availment of input tax credit & non-reversal of ITC on exempted supplies for the period April 2021 to March 2022. Further the order in appeal has been passed for allowance of ₹ 6.36 million and appeal rejected for amount of ₹ 44.05 million. The company is in the process of filing appeal before GSTAT. b) During the Financial year 2025-26, the company has received a GST order for an amount ₹ 42.48 million for irregular availment of ITC during the period from April 2020 to March 2021 on exempted prouduct and irregular availment of ITC on freezer, refrigerator and cooler during the period April 2020 to March 2023. Further the order in appeal has been passed for allowance of ₹ 21.36 million and appeal rejected for amount of ₹ 21.12 million. The company is in the process of filing appeal before GSTAT.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Commissioner of GST and Central Excise, Salem
tax_litigation.status: Provisional acknowledgement for the appeal filed before GSTAT was received and awaiting for further proceedings/ hearing+H14

operating_notes.text: Company opted for the 25.168% tax regime under Section 200 of the Income Tax Act, 2025 (erstwhile Section 115BAA) from 1 April 2026, remeasuring deferred tax in Q1FY27.
2,50,00,000 CCPS of ₹2 each issued to Jongsong Investments Pte. Ltd. converted into equity on 22 July 2026.
Business is a single reportable segment: processing of milk and manufacturing of milk-related products.
Perundurai facility FY26 capacity utilisation: paneer 114%, cheddar 110%, yogurt 89%, ghee 72%, khoa 70%; paneer capacity raised to 192 MT/day in June 2025 and cheddar to 120 MT/day.
Milk procurement was ~13 LLPD from 83,000+ farmers across ~3,000 milk collection units as of March 31, 2026.
E-commerce share of revenue rose to 13.70% in FY26 from 7.51% in FY24, with e-commerce revenue up 214% to ₹429.96 Cr.
Q1FY27 daily average milk procurement was 13.2 lakh litres; landed cost ₹45/litre with ₹41-42 paid to farmers and partner MilkLane at about 10-12% of volumes.
Own logistics of 375 vehicles plus reverse-haul loads save about 18-20% on logistics cost.
Trade discount from MRP to billing is about 4.5-5% and marketing/promotion another 4.5-5%.
Q1FY27 average daily milk procurement stood at 13.2 lakh litres per day (LLPD), up 28% YoY.
Perundurai plant current revenue potential estimated at 3x to 3.5x of FY26 numbers based on current pricing.
Regional revenue mix stands at 69% South and 31% non-South.
New Skyr and Greek Yogurt plant commissioned at Perundurai facility with capacity of 150 tonnes per day and investment of ₹40 Cr, effective September 10, 2026
New Skyr and Greek Yogurt plant at Perundurai has processing capacity of up to 150 tonnes/day, against about 20 tonnes/day for the 2022 multi-product yogurt facility.
Annual demand for the yogurt category has grown more than 50% since 2022, and high-protein yogurt demand has more than doubled in recent months.
The ₹40 Cr Skyr and Greek Yogurt plant is part of the Perundurai expansion programme and one of the stated objects of the company's IPO.
Milky Mist commissioned a new 10 MW solar power plant at Arasanoor on September 30, 2026, increasing total renewable capacity to 41 MW.
Total investment in the 25 MW solar capacity at Arasanoor is approximately ₹109.60 crore.
Cumulative investment in renewable energy plants is close to ₹197 crore for 41 MW capacity.
Milky Mist launched High Protein Lactose-free Milk in a 250 ml pack delivering 25g of protein.

Milky Mist's Q1FY27 earnings call on September 1, 2026 disclosed a 10.5% price hike, ₹700 Cr RHP capex, a whey protein plant in 15-18 months and a Maharashtra plant about three years away.
Milky Mist held its Q1FY27 concall, reporting 44% YoY revenue growth to ₹973.45 Cr and outlining plans to deploy 50,000+ coolers over 3 years.
